extracted.intended_audience: plant breeders, applicants, IP practitioners, and state administrative authorities handling plant variety protection in Vietnam
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and evaluation criteria for obtaining, maintaining, cancelling, and enforcing plant variety protection in Vietnam, including DUS testing, denomination rules, application contents, procedure timelines, rights and limitations, licensing and compulsory licensing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniformity of the plant variety
rubrics_metrics.description: The variety shall be deemed to have uniformity in the propagation if there is the same expression of the relevant phenotype unless the variation is permitted for certain characteristic in its propagation process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uniformity is assessed by consistent expression of relevant phenotypic characteristics across propagated material; permitted variations in propagation processes are allowed where explicitly accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stability of the plant variety
rubrics_metrics.description: The variety shall be deemed to be stable if the relevant phenotypic characteristics of that variety retain the same expression as originally described, and remain unchanged after each propagation crop or propagation cycle, as the case may be.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stability requires that characteristics described at grant persist unchanged over successive propagation cycles; this is a criterion evaluated in technical testing (DUS).

rubrics_metrics.name: Denomination: proposed name requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The registrant must propose an appropriate name for the plant variety which name must be the same as the denomination registered in any country upon filing of a protection registration application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed denomination should match any denomination previously registered in other countries at time of filing; registrant is responsible for proposing an appropriate, consistent name.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denomination: distinctiveness requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The variety shall be deemed to be properly denominated if it is distinguishable from all other varieties of common knowledge in the same species or similar species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Denomination must uniquely identify the variety vis-à-vis other known varieties in same or similar species to avoid confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited/Improper denominations
rubrics_metrics.description: Denominations shall not be considered proper if they: consist only of numerals (except where numerals relate to particularity/establishment); violate social morality; are liable to misrepresent features; are easy to misunderstand about Breeder’s identification; are identical or confusingly similar to a protected trademark/trade name/geographical indication existing before filing; are identical/similar to names of harvested products; or affect prior rights of others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A list of concrete prohibitions on variety names to prevent misleading or rights-conflicting denominations; includes trademark/geographical indication conflicts and moral/representational restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of variety name in commerce after protection expires
rubrics_metrics.description: Any organization or individual that offers for sale or brings to market propagating materials of the plant variety must use the name of the plant variety as the name in the Protection Certificate even after the expiry of the protection period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obligation for sellers/marketers to continue using the certificate name to maintain traceability and consistency in the market.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combining denomination with trademarks
rubrics_metrics.description: When the name of a plant variety is combined with a trademark, trade name or an indication similar to the name of plant variety already registered for sale or offer in the market, such name must be easily distinctive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a variety name is used together with a trademark, the combined labeling must be clearly distinctive to avoid consumer confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may be registrant
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants include: (a) the breeder who directly bred or discovered and developed the variety by their own efforts and expenses; (b) organizations or individuals who invested for the breeder under contract (unless otherwise agreed); (c) organizations or individuals who have transferred or inherited the right of registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines legal entitlement to file; transfers and contractual arrangements must be documented.

rubrics_metrics.name: State ownership for varieties bred with state funding
rubrics_metrics.description: For plant varieties bred or discovered using State budget or project finance under State management, rights over such plant variety will belong to the State; Government shall provide specific provisions for registration in those cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special rule allocating ownership to the State when public funds/resources were used; procedural specifics delegated to government regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file (national and foreign applicants)
rubrics_metrics.description: Vietnamese organizations/individuals or foreign organizations/individuals with a permanent address or a plant variety business/production establishment in Vietnam may file directly or via legal representative; foreigners without such presence must file through a lawful representative in Vietnam.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies filing eligibility and requirement of local representation for applicants without presence in Vietnam.

rubrics_metrics.name: First applicant / priority among multiple applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: If more than one independent person submits applications on different days, the certificate will be given to the applicant with the earliest valid registration; if multiple applications for the same variety are submitted the same day, the certificate goes to the registrant agreed by all; if no agreement, to the first breeder who bred/discovered/developed the variety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority rules for competing filings; uses filing date and breeder status to resolve same-day conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority claim and documentation (12-month rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrant may request priority rights if an application for the same variety was submitted within 12 months in a country that and Vietnam both enter into an agreement on plant variety protection. The filing date of the first application is excluded from the 12-month calculation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To claim priority registrant must specify the claim in the application and, within 3 months of filing, produce certified copies and evidence proving the varieties are the same and pay fees; can supply information to the authority later depending on species and circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of Plant Variety Protection Certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: A Protection Certificate must include: name of the variety and species; name of the right holder (Certificate Holder) and Breeder’s name; duration of protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines mandatory certificate contents to be recorded and entered into the National Registration Book.

rubrics_metrics.name: Territorial effect and term of protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Protection applies throughout Vietnam; term is 25 years for trees and grapes, 20 years for other species, effective from grant date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines scope in territory and species-specific terms of protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation grounds for protection certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: Certificate may be cancelled if: (a) uniformity and stability no longer meet requirements as at grant time; (b) Certificate Holder does not pay annual fees; (c) Holder does not supply necessary documents and propagating materials for maintaining as prescribed; (d) Holder does not change the plant variety name as requested by the authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates concrete grounds that permit cancellation; both substantive (DUS) and procedural/administrative grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation procedures and reinstatement timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: For non-DUS or name-change/document-supply cases, authority issues cancellation decision; for non-payment, cancellation effective from first date of next effective year where fees unpaid. Holder has right to request explanation and must pay fee to reinstate; holder must solve reasons within 90 days from filing for reinstatement in certain cases. For DUS-ground cancellations, reinstatement requires proving DUS compliance and certification by the authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies notification, publication, deadlines (30 days to request explanation after publication of cancellation, 90 days to remedy certain causes), fee requirements and evidentiary standard for reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nullity of protection certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: Certificate will be nullified if: (a) application belonged to an applicant without the right to file (unless right later assigned); (b) protected variety did not meet novelty or distinctness at time of grant; (c) protected variety did not meet uniformity or stability where grant was based on registrant-supplied test results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nullity retroactively invalidates the certificate; transactions based on the right become null and void and handled under Civil Law; any party may request nullity during the certificate's effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction and re-issuance of certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: Holder may request changes/rectification of errors in name/address of holder (fees payable); authority must rectify errors made by it (and may recover fees); holder may request re-issue if certificate is lost or damaged (fees payable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative remedy provisions for correcting certificate data and re-issuing lost/damaged certificates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: All decisions related to grant, re-issue, cancellation, nullity, amendment of the variety protection certificate shall be published by the State management office in a specialized bulletin within 60 days from decision date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandatory publication timeline to ensure transparency and public notice of status changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application contents (required documents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Application must include: prescribed registration form; photos and technical questionnaires using prescribed form; authorization if filed through a representative; documents demonstrating registration right if registrant is assignee; documents to prove priority if claiming priority; and receipt of fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete documentation is required for acceptance; missing items can trigger invalidity or correction requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language requirements for application documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications and transactions must be in Vietnamese, except that certain documents (power of attorney, documents evidencing registration right, documents evidencing priority, other documents) may be in another language but must be translated into Vietnamese at the authority's request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies language of record and permitted exceptions with translation requirement on request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documents to prove priority
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents include a copy of the first application certified by the authorized organization, and paper of transfer/inheritance of priority right if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets evidentiary documents necessary to substantiate a priority claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing date for the application is the date on which the application is received by the State management office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear rule for determining official filing date (receipt by authority).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination of validity within 15 days
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 15 days from the filing date, the authority will examine the application to determine its validity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short statutory validity check period (15 days) to confirm completeness and basic eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for considering an application invalid
rubrics_metrics.description: An application is invalid if: (a) it does not follow requirements; (b) the variety does not belong to a species in the List of protected species; (c) the registrant does not have the right to file (including when co-rights exist but one owner does not agree).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates the three core invalidity triggers on procedural and substantive grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures following validity examination
rubrics_metrics.description: If invalid due to species or right-to-file, announce refusal with reasons; if invalid due to form errors, inform registrant to correct within 30 days; if registrant fails to correct or give reasonable appeal, refuse; if application is valid (or corrected), accept and request samples for technical test following Article 178.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies notification content, 30-day correction window, and next steps (technical testing) upon acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of accepted application (90-day rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application is valid, the authority shall publish it in the specialized bulletin on plant varieties within 90 days from the date the application is accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication contents must include application number, filing date, representative agent (if any), registrant name, owner name, variety name, species, and date accepted as valid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination of application content: novelty and denomination and technical test
rubrics_metrics.description: The authority shall examine novelty and denomination and examine results of the Technical Test of the variety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical Test results (DUS) are central to substantive examination; novelty and correct denomination are also evaluated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical Test definition and conduct (DUS testing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical Test means conducting growing tests to determine distinctness, uniformity and stability (DUS). The test shall be carried out by competent offices/organizations/individuals with enough capacity following Ministry stipulations. The authority may use prior technical test results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DUS testing procedures must meet ministry rules; previous valid test results may be relied upon; competence of testing body matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for examining technical test results (90 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: The time for examining the test results shall be 90 days from the date of receiving the technical test results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies a 90-day statutory period for the authority to examine technical test outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modification/supplementation rights before decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Before decision to grant or refuse, registrant may modify or amend the application without changing its nature; may request acknowledgment of changes of name/address; may request acknowledgement of changes of registrant due to transfer or inheritance. Fees apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows applicants limited amendments and post-filing changes (with fees) until decision is made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of application and fee refund
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrant may withdraw the application in writing before decision; upon withdrawal all subsequent procedures terminate and fees submitted for unperformed procedures will be refunded upon registrant request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides for voluntary withdrawal and partial fee refund for unexecuted steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party opinions during pendency
rubrics_metrics.description: From publication of the application until decision, any third party may send a written opinion about granting the certificate to the authority, accompanied by arguments and evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public participation mechanism allowing third parties to submit objections or evidence during pendency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal to grant: procedure and opportunity to amend/appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: An application shall be refused if the variety does not meet conditions in Articles 176 (validity) and 178 (examination). On refusal the authority shall announce a proposal to refuse stating reasons and a deadline for registrant to amend shortcomings or appeal; if not remedied, announce refusal; if amendments/appeal valid, proceed as in grant procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides procedural safeguards: proposal-to-refuse notice, opportunity to amend or appeal before final refusal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Granting and recording of protection certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: If not refused and the registrant pays the fee, the authority shall issue decision granting the certificate and record it into the National Registration Book of Protected Plant Varieties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grant is conditioned on no outstanding refusals and payment of prescribed fee; mandatory recording in national register follows grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of complaint against grant/refusal
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrant and any third party have the right to complain about a decision to grant or refuse a certificate; complaints are carried out according to the Law on Complaints and Denunciations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative remedy channel for disputing grant/refusal decisions under general complaints law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breeder rights (moral/economic entitlements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Breeder's name will be recorded on the protection certificate, National Register and published documents; breeder is entitled to compensation as stipulated in law (cross-ref Article 191).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes breeder attribution and entitlement to compensation; recording is mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights of Protection Certificate Holder (acts of exploitation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Holder has rights to use or permit others to use propagation materials for: production/multiplication; processing for propagation; offering for sale; selling/marketing; exporting; importing; stocking for these purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comprehensive list of exclusive acts the certificate-holder controls over propagating materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to prohibit uses (enforcement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Holder can prohibit others from using the plant variety in accordance with infringement provisions (Article 188).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Holder's exclusionary rights enable enforcement actions against unauthorized use subject to infringement rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer, inheritance and assignment of rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Holder may pass rights by inheritance, bequest or transfer in accordance with law; assignment transfers all rights to assignee who becomes owner from registration of assignment; assignment under co-ownership requires consent of all owners; assignments must be in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formalities for transfer/assignment are specified (written form, registration); co-ownership adds unanimous consent requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of rights to derived varieties and those not clearly different
rubrics_metrics.description: Holder's rights extend to varieties originating from the protected variety (retaining essential characteristics), varieties not clearly different from the protected variety, and varieties whose production requires repeated use of the protected variety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines scope of derived and essentially similar varieties covered by holder's exclusive rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acts constituting infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: Infringements include: exploiting/using holder's rights without permission; using a denomination identical or similar to a protected denomination of same or similar species; using the protected variety without payment of required compensation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three enumerated infringement types covering unauthorized exploitation, confusing denomination use, and unpaid exploitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary rights from publication until grant
rubrics_metrics.description: Temporary rights arise from publication of the registration application until grant date (unless certificate not granted). Registrant may notify commercial users in writing specifying submission and publication dates; notified users continuing to exploit must pay an amount equivalent to value of transfer of the right to use within an appropriate scope/time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects registrant's interests during pendency via notification and compensation mechanism for continued commercial exploitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations/exceptions to holder's rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Not considered infringement: private non-commercial use; use for breeding or scientific research; use to create new distinct varieties; production households using harvested products of protected variety for propagation and cultivation in their own field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates farmer's privilege and research/breeding exceptions; clarifies non-infringing activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhaustion / limits after sale or export
rubrics_metrics.description: Rights do not extend to acts related to materials of the protected variety that have been sold or otherwise taken out of the Vietnamese or overseas market by the breeder or nominee, except for continuous propagation of such variety or export to a country where the genus/species is not protected (unless exported for consumption only).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines post-sale/exhaustion limits and exceptions for propagation/export to non-protecting countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligations of Certificate Holder
rubrics_metrics.description: Holder must: pay compensation to the breeder as agreed or per law if not agreed; pay fees for the protection certificate; preserve the protected variety and supply propagating material to the state authority and maintain the stability of the protected variety as prescribed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Holder has both financial and stewardship obligations, including supplying material for official purposes and maintaining DUS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligations of the Breeder
rubrics_metrics.description: Breeder must help the protection certificate holder to maintain propagating material of the protected variety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cooperative duty for breeder to assist in preservation/maintenance of propagating material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensing formalities and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensing means permission by holder to another to conduct one or more acts; licensing requires consent of all holders in co-ownership; must be in a written contract; licensing contracts must not unreasonably restrict licensee rights, particularly provisions not deriving from or aimed at protecting licensor's rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies formality (written), co-ownership unanimity, and anti-abusive clause preventing unreasonable restrictions on licensees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights and remedies in licensing contracts (licensor/licensee)
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensor may permit or refuse licensee to assign the license to third parties. Licensee may assign only if agreed by licensor; may request licensor to take measures against third-party infringements causing damage to licensee; may act if licensor fails to act within 3 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocates procedural rights and enforcement responsibilities between licensor and licensee, including fallback for licensee to act if licensor neglects enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment formalities
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignment transfers all rights to the assignee who becomes owner from the date of registration of the assignment contract with the authority; assignment under co-ownership requires consent of all owners; must be in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reiterates registration and written-form requirements for valid assignment and co-ownership consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compulsory licensing: grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority may grant compulsory licenses without holder consent where: (a) use is for public interest/non-commercial purposes (national defense, security, disease prevention/treatment, nutrition, urgent social needs); (b) a person needing capacity to use fails to reach agreement despite best efforts to negotiate price and terms; (c) holder is conducting acts constraining competition under competition law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates public interest, failure to negotiate, and anti-competitive conduct as grounds for compulsory licensing; public-interest uses prioritized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compulsory licensing: conditions and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Compulsory license conditions: right of use is non-exclusive; scope and period limited to objectives and primarily for domestic market supply (except 195.1(c)); licensee cannot assign or sublicense (except with business assignment); licensee must pay adequate compensation considering economic value and government remuneration framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compulsory licenses are narrowly tailored, non-transferable/sub-licensable, limited in time/scope and require compensation per government rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority and procedure for compulsory licensing
rubrics_metrics.description: Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development issues decisions on licensing for uses under its state administration; other ministries may issue decisions in their fields after consultation; licensing decision must fix scope/conditions; authority must notify holder; decision/ refusal may be complained about or litigated; Government provides detailed procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies institutional competence, consultation, mandatory notice to holder, and availability of administrative/judicial review; procedural details delegated to Government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights of holder subject to compulsory licensing
rubrics_metrics.description: Holder subject to compulsory license has right to receive adequate compensation corresponding to economic value or equivalent contractual price; may request amendment/cancellation/nullification of compulsory license when bases cease to exist provided such change is not prejudicial to licensee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects holders by guaranteeing compensation and providing mechanisms to rescind compulsory licenses when justifications lapse, subject to protecting licensee interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to protection measures and remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: IP right holders may take measures: technological measures to prevent infringement; request infringers to terminate acts, apologize, publicly rectify and compensate damages; request competent state agencies to handle infringements; initiate lawsuits in competent court or arbitrator. Organizations/individuals suffering damage or discovering harmful infringements may request state agencies to handle infringements that damage consumers or society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists enforcement options: technical protection, administrative requests, civil litigation, and reporting to authorities for consumer/societal harms.
